creative_intent: Precision material study of a matte white boron-carbide ceramic industrial component, emphasizing tactile density and subtle surface variation within a clean, engineered object context.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

constraints: even illumination to highlight material properties
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Loss of manufactured object readability due to material focus.
Drift towards abstract forms or texture-only output.
Introduction of forbidden material reads or finishes.
Subject appearing decorative, organic, or consumer-gadget like.
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Ensure material read is dry, dense, and technical ceramic.
Prevent any interpretation as plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish.
Strictly avoid abstract, atmospheric, or texture-only compositions.
Protect the manufactured object identity at all costs, even within a material study.
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
success_criteria: Immediate recognition of a matte white boron-carbide technical ceramic material.
Clear readability of a precision-manufactured industrial component.
Evidence of tactile ceramic density and subtle mineral surface variation.
Absence of any forbidden material reads or finishes.
The object must appear engineered, non-decorative, and non-organic.
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
direction_summary: Focus on rendering a clean, matte white boron-carbide technical ceramic material on a precision-manufactured industrial component. The primary goal is a material study, ensuring the ceramic's dry, dense, and engineered qualities are paramount, while maintaining a clear, non-decorative manufactured object identity. Suppress all forbidden material reads and finishes.
